newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer but off highs, 125.00 seen heavy.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer but off highs, 125.00 seen heavy.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended a slow day firmer but off earlier highs, traders said on Monday.

Noting that strong technical resistance had developed near 125.20, a trader with a bank's securities arm said that without any fresh factors, buying aggressive enough to lift the key contract over 125 was unlikely at this point.

Bargain-hunting by traders and a general sense of relief after morning statements from Bank of Japan (BOJ) head Yasuo Matsushita produced nothing new helped buoy the contract, which ended at 124.96 against 124.91 in Friday Tokyo trade.
Volume was a thin 21,748 contracts, which traders said also contributed to the contract's rise by exaggerating price movements. The key September contract ranged from 124.71 to 124.99.
Morning strength in the Tokyo stock market prompted sales of bonds in early trade, but losses were erased by midday after Matsushita's comments prompted short-covering, traders said.

Matsushita told a meeting of the BOJ's branch officers on Monday that the Japanese economy is continuing on a gradual recovery trend supported by firm production and incomes despite a lingering impact from April's consumption tax rise.
Public-sector investment is on a declining trend but net exports are continuing to increase, he said in a statement.
"There is little possibility that the recovery trend itself will falter," Matsushita said in the statement.
"There was a bit of a feeling in the market that Matsushita might say something bullish about the economy, and relief that he did not sparked short-covering," one trader said.
But he added that the market will continue to watch the two-day branch managers meeting for further statements on Tuesday.
Otherwise, trade this week is likely to be quiet.
"The market will be watching for key trade figures from both Japan and the U.S. at the end of the week, with the response of the currency markets perhaps leading bond markets," one trader said.
Activity in cash bonds was also quiet, with the benchmark 182nd 10-year cash bond standing unchanged from Friday's close at 2.280 percent after having moved narrowly from 2.275 to 2.300 percent.
